TEHRAN — A U.S. Army officer says he warned senior commanders that Iranian drones could hit their makeshift outpost in Kuwait, and on the second day of the war on Iran that began on Feb. 28, one drone did, killing six American soldiers. An investigation by CBS News’ flagship program 60 Minutes, broadcast Sunday, counts that strike among at least 31 successful Iranian attacks on U.S. military installations and ostensibly “diplomatic” sites across eight countries, a category that includes CIA stations operating under diplomatic cover. The Pentagon has never fully laid out the extent of that damage. Before the war, the Pentagon pulled about 90 percent of its ground forces out of Kuwait, fearing retaliation. About 70 members of the Army Reserve’s 103rd Sustainment Command, a logistics unit, were sent the other way, to a small outpost within reach of short-range Iranian drones. Stephen Ramsbottom, the unit’s deputy chief of operations, says some called it a “trailer park.” Its defenses were built for car bombs. “There was nothing there designed to protect from an aerial attack.” Six soldiers told 60 Minutes they had seen U.S. intelligence that supposedly put Port Shuaiba on an Iranian target list. US military command ‘killed my wife’ “There was definitely an X where we were,” Ramsbottom said. He says he warned John Hinson, the Central Command logistics chief, and was told, “We don’t have to worry about protection.” A counter-drone system mentioned the week before never showed up.

Philippine authorities arrested nearly 300 people as thousands of demonstrators poured into the streets of Manila to protest U.S. President Donald Trump’s visit, prompting a heavy security crackdown across the capital. Trump arrived in Manila on Tuesday to attend the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) summit, drawing protests over his administration’s policies, the economic fallout from the U.S.-Israeli war on Iran, and a U.S.-led initiative on artificial intelligence and critical minerals. Organizers said up to 10,000 people were expected to join the protests, with demonstrators planning to march toward the Philippine International Convention Center, where the summit is being held, Press TV reported. On Tuesday, police blocked protesters attempting to reach the venue, while security measures for the summit led to the closure of large sections of central Manila. Demonstrators repeatedly chanted the slogan “Trump Out,” demanding that the US president leave the country. On Monday, protesters burned effigies of Trump and clashed with police officers carrying batons and shields. They also held placards describing the U.S. president as the world’s “No. 1 terrorist.”

TEHRAN- Grand Ayatollah Sheikh Hossein Vahid Khorasani, one of the most prominent Shiite religious authorities and Islamic scholars, has passed away at the age of 105. His office announced his death in a statement expressing profound sorrow, describing him as an eminent jurist of the Ahl al-Bayt (the family of Prophet Muhammad, PBUH), a distinguished Shiite religious authority, a devout scholar and a renowned teacher at Islamic seminaries. Born on January 1, 1921, Ayatollah Vahid Khorasani devoted decades to the study, research and teaching of Islamic sciences. Over the course of his scholarly career, he educated generations of prominent religious scholars and played a significant role in preserving Islamic traditions and religious ceremonies. The senior cleric had recently been hospitalized in Tehran. Representatives of Leader of the Islamic Revolution Ayatollah Seyyed Mojtaba Hosseini Khamenei had visited him during his hospitalization. His passing marks the loss of a highly influential figure in contemporary Shiite scholarship and religious learning.

Теперь центром экономических процессов, промышленным и технологическим хабом планеты стал Азиатско-Тихоокеанский регион.
